newsitem.title: USA: Dow, S&P swept to record highs in broad rally.
newsitem.headline: Dow, S&P swept to record highs in broad rally.

text.p: Wall Street stocks stormed higher on Wednesday, sparked by a resurgent technology sector, a strong dollar and powerful mutual fund inflows.

The Dow industrials rose 103.52 points to close unofficially at 6961.63, the average's first finish above the 6900 mark. If official, the gain would stand as the fifth-largest in point terms in the Dow's history.
The sweeping rally left few sectors behind. Technology, financial, energy and gold mining, and transportation shares all surged.

Analysts said the sudden burst of confidence had its roots in the technology sector, which got a critical boost when semiconductor equipment maker Applied Materials Inc reported stronger-than-expected first-quarter earnings.
The earnings, announced late Tuesday, triggered a sharp jump in technology stocks that quickly spread to the broader market.
"The Applied Materials results definitely helped," said Bill Meehan, a market analyst at Prudential Securities.

"If you step back and look, we spent a good deal of January ratcheting up interest rates and that didn't break the market," Meehan said. "Then we got some technology disappointments, and even in the face of those we're having a strong rebound."

The resurgent tech sector pushed the Nasdaq Composite index .IXIC two percent higher, while the Nasdaq 100 .NDX, which includes the composite's largest stocks, rose 3.3 percent. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose a sizzling 6.75 percent, led by Applied Materials, which surged seven points to 52-1/8.

The renewed appetite for stocks came amid fresh reports that investors were pouring more cash into U.S. stock mutual funds. The Investment Company Institute on Wednesday said net cash flows into such funds nearly doubled in January to $24 billion from $12.22 billion in December.

After a brief slowdown early this month, investment resumed its breakneck pace, with cash inflows into U.S. equity funds jumping to $1.2 billion in the two-day period ended February 10, according to a survey by Mutual Fund Trim Tabs.
The survey showed that during the three days ended February 6, inflows amounted to only $4 million.
Also lending support was the ever firming dollar, which worked its way still higher today, gaining ground against both the German mark and the Japanese yen.

Concern has been raised about the impact of a strong dollar on earnings for U.S. multinational corporations, but analysts said the currency's rise had broader implications that far overshadowed those worries.
"The more important factor is that a strong dollar has induced foreign investors to buy U.S. securities," said Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson Lane.
"The big picture is that the flood of foreign money is far more important than the earnings implications for most of the market," he said.

Gold prices jumped in New York Commodity Exchange activity, helping gold mining shares to one of their best sessions in weeks. Newmont Mining Corp gained 2-1/4 to 41-1/4 and Homestake Mining Co rose 7/8 to 14-3/4.
Energy shares continued to rebound from their recent weakness. Exxon Corp climbed 1-3/8 to 103, Texaco Inc rose 1-3/8 to 104-3/4 and Chevron Corp jumped 2-3/8 to 69-1/8.

Banks and brokerage stocks also posted solid gains, even as the bond market finished the session essentially unchanged. Charles Schwab Corp rose two to 39-1/4, Salomon Inc rose 1-3/8 to 59-3/8, Citicorp gained 1-3/4 to 119-1/2 and NationsBank Corp climbed 1-7/8 to 115-1/4.
Converse Inc rose 4-3/8 to 20-5/8 after a federal court approved the bankruptcy plan of its Aplx One Inc unit and Smith Barney upgraded the shares to buy from outperform.
Money Store Inc surged 5-1/8 to 26-3/8 after the loan company's earnings beat Wall Street forecasts.
The Nasdaq Composite gained 27.45 to 1358.96. The increase was the index's fourth largest ever in point terms.
The S&P 500 rose 13.18 points to a record 802.77.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
(( -- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721))
